# Drishti Elements

<p align="center"><picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="brand/drishti_elements-logo-light.svg"><img src="brand/drishti_elements-logo.svg" alt="Drishti Elements" height="64"></picture></p>

**Drishti Elements** is a set of plain JavaScript libraries for data-heavy screens: a grid with a pivot, charts and maps, inputs and forms, a data
client, trees, graphs and a designer kit. No framework, no build step, no CDN, and no server needed.

> **Proprietary. Copyright (c) 2026 Ashutosh Sinha. All rights reserved.** This repository is visible to the public, but no licence is granted: you may
> not copy, use, modify or distribute this code without the copyright holder's written permission. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). Third-party libraries under
> `vendor/` keep their own licences, listed in [vendor/VENDOR.md](vendor/VENDOR.md). Contributions are not accepted at this time.

## The libraries

<!-- libraries: generated by tools/docs/elements_api.py from the manifest; do not edit -->

| Library | What it is | Requires |
|---|---|---|
| [`drishti-core`](docs/API.md#drishti-core) | Formats, theme tokens, the API client, events, accessibility, dialogs, toasts, the state kit, the command palette and the loader | nothing |
| [`drishti-inputs`](docs/API.md#drishti-inputs) | Date and range pickers, multi-select, combobox, forms from a schema, the filter bar, the code editor | `drishti-core` |
| [`drishti-grid`](docs/API.md#drishti-grid) | The grid and its pivot: virtual rows, tree data, ranges, editing, live sets, export, an AG Grid-style adapter | `drishti-core`, `drishti-inputs`, `drishti-chart` |
| [`drishti-tree`](docs/API.md#drishti-tree) | Hierarchies as a tree grid, an org chart, a sunburst or an icicle, with measures and an edit mode | `drishti-core`, `drishti-inputs`, `drishti-grid` |
| [`drishti-designer`](docs/API.md#drishti-designer) | The designer kit: layout canvas, palette, inspector, outline, YAML pane, undo and redo, the designer shell | `drishti-core`, `drishti-inputs`, `drishti-tree` |
| [`drishti-data`](docs/API.md#drishti-data) | One data-source contract (memory, REST, server-side rows, Arrow, live) and the Arrow client | `drishti-core` |
| [`drishti-chart`](docs/API.md#drishti-chart) | One chart spec over ECharts: the general kinds, maps from the world to first-level regions, Explain, export | `drishti-core`, `drishti-inputs` |
| [`drishti-graph`](docs/API.md#drishti-graph) | Networks on a canvas for thousands of nodes: layouts, paths, groups, selection, an adjacency table | `drishti-core`, `drishti-inputs`, `drishti-grid` |
| [`drishti-events`](docs/API.md#drishti-events) | Events in the page, across tabs and with a server: topics, publish and subscribe, request and reply, streams | `drishti-core` |
| [`drishti-views`](docs/API.md#drishti-views) | Whole screens from a ViewModel: the specification and its validator, the painter and every kind, live frames, &lt;elements-view&gt;, the builders | `drishti-core` |

<!-- /libraries -->

Each library is ES modules under `elements/<library>/src/` and one bundled classic script. [elements/drishti_elements.json](elements/drishti_elements.json)
is the one list.

## Quick start for a plain HTML page

Serve a copy of the release tree (`python3 tools/elements/cli.py dist`) from your own web server, then:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/vendor/drishti/css/drishti_tokens.css">
<script src="/vendor/drishti/elements/drishti-core/drishti_core.js"></script>
<div id="grid" style="height: 260px"></div>
<script>
  Drishti.elements.load('drishti-grid').then(() => {
    new Drishti.elements.grid.Grid(document.getElementById('grid'), {
      columns: [{ field: 'desk', header: 'Desk' }, { field: 'pnl', header: 'P&L', type: 'number', format: 'amount0' }],
      rows: [{ desk: 'Rates', pnl: 1250000 }, { desk: 'Credit', pnl: -340000 }, { desk: 'FX', pnl: 560000 }],
      getRowId: (r) => r.desk,
    });
  });
</script>
```

More in [docs/USING.md](docs/USING.md) (the widgets), [docs/VIEWS.md](docs/VIEWS.md) (the painter), [docs/EVENTS.md](docs/EVENTS.md) and four runnable [tutorials](docs/TUTORIALS.md).

## The gallery

Every component live, with its options, its events and the code to use it: the docs site at https://ajsinha.github.io/drishti-elements/. To open it locally,
build the release tree and serve it:

```bash
python3 tools/elements/cli.py dist --out dist
cd dist/drishti-elements-3.3.1 && python3 -m http.server 8765      # then open /gallery/drishti_gallery.html
```

## Versioning

One version for every library, semantic versioning, today **3.3.1** (`elements` in [elements/drishti_elements.json](elements/drishti_elements.json)). What
changed is in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).

## Browser support

The current and previous major versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari. No build step and no framework are needed. CI tests Chromium.

## Build and test

```bash
python3 tools/elements/build.py --check && python3 tools/docs/elements_api.py --check && python3 tools/license_headers.py
python3 tools/run_tests.py               # the standard test command: parallel run, then the budget tests alone, serially; fails on any skip
                                         # needs: pip install -r tests/requirements.txt && python3 -m playwright install chromium (pinned: Playwright 1.64.0)
```

The performance-budget tests (a rate or a time limit: pytest marker `budget`, Node tests named `budget: ...`) never run beside other work:
`tools/run_tests.py` runs everything else in parallel (`node tools/node_tests.mjs tests/elements`, then `pytest -n 8 -m "not budget"`), then the
budget tests one at a time. The browsers are required: a missing Playwright or Chromium fails the run with the install command, and so does any skipped test.

`python3 tools/elements/build.py` rewrites the bundles after a change to a module (offline, Python only).

## Build and run in the IDE

No Java here: Python and Node only. The launchers are checked in and visible.

| IDE | What runs what |
|---|---|
| **PyCharm** (open this folder) | `run-configs/`, folder **Elements**, names `Elements: <verb> <what>`: build all, build dist, check bundles / API docs / licence headers, test, test static, test one file, and the Maven launchers (`pom.xml`, exec-maven-plugin) `test Node` and `run gallery server` |
| **IntelliJ IDEA Community** | no Python and no Node/JavaScript support: the two Maven launchers (`Elements: test Node`, `Elements: run gallery server`; Node and Python on the PATH, no bash), PyCharm or VS Code for the rest |
| **VS Code** | **File, Open Workspace from File**, `drishti-elements.code-workspace`: tasks (checks, build, dist, Node and pytest suites, gallery server) and Run and Debug configurations; recommended extensions: Python and Pylance, ESLint, YAML |

Prepare once: `pip install -r tests/requirements.txt` and `playwright install chromium`. Windows: use `python` for `python3`; the Maven launchers need no bash (name the programs with `-Dnode=` / `-Dpython=` when they are not on the PATH). Elements needs no Java and no `~/.m2` artefact itself. The family's install order is Rachana (tag), then the tools, then Lake (tag), then Drishti; the Rachana and Lake jars land in
`~/.m2/repository/com/ash/{rachana,lake}/` (Windows `C:\Users\<user>\.m2\repository`) (Elements itself is not a Maven artefact). The installation order, JDK 21 and the local Maven repository are described once, in [Drishti Rachana's java/README](https://github.com/ajsinha/drishti-rachana/blob/g2/integration/java/README.md#build-and-run-in-the-ide).
